name: hello
program:
' Hello, world. Text between quotes is printed; ! inside quotes is a newline.
"Hello, world!"
$$

name: arithmetic
program:
' Postfix arithmetic: operands first, then the operator.
"3 + 4       = " 3 4 + ! "!"
"10 - 4      = " 10 4 - ! "!"
"6 * 7       = " 6 7 * ! "!"
"17 / 5      = " 17 5 / ! "!"          ' division truncates
"(2 + 3) * 4 = " 2 3 + 4 * ! "!"
"2 + 3 * 4   = " 2 3 4 * + ! "!"
"-7          = " 0 7 - ! "!"           ' there is no unary minus
$$

name: variables
program:
' A letter pushes the ADDRESS of a variable. Use . to fetch the value
' and = to store one:  address value =
X 17 =                     ' X := 17
Y X. 2 * =                 ' Y := X * 2
"X = " X. ! "!"
"Y = " Y. ! "!"
"The address of X is " X ! " and of Y is " Y ! "!"
$$

name: countdown
program:
' A loop is ( ... ). The ^ operator pops a value and leaves the loop
' when it is zero or negative.
N 10 =
( N. ^                     ' while N > 0
  N. ! " "
  N N. 1 - = )             ' N := N - 1
"Lift off!!"
$$

name: conditions
program:
' A condition is  value [ ... ]  and runs the bracket when value > 0.
' Mouse only tests "greater than zero", so other tests are built from it.
"Enter a number: " N ? = "!"
N. [ "positive!" ]                         ' N > 0
0 N. - [ "negative!" ]                     ' N < 0
1 N. + [ 1 N. - [ "zero!" ] ]              ' N = 0  (N > -1 and N < 1)
N. 9 - [ "bigger than nine!" ]             ' N > 9
10 N. - [ "less than ten!" ]               ' N < 10
$$

name: fibonacci
program:
' The first N Fibonacci numbers.
"How many terms? " N ? = "!"
A 0 = B 1 =
( N. ^
  A. ! " "
  T A. B. + =  A B. =  B T. =
  N N. 1 - = )
"!"
$$

name: factorial
program:
' Factorial three ways: a loop, a loop inside a macro, and recursion.
"N: " N ? = "!"
F 1 = I N. =
( I. ^ F F. I. * = I I. 1 - = )
"loop:      " F. ! "!"
"macro:     " #L,N.; ! "!"
"recursive: " #F,N.; ! "!"

$L N %A = 1 ( N. ^ N. * N N. 1 - = ) @
$F %A [ %A #F,%A 1 -; * @ ] 1 @
$$

name: fizzbuzz
program:
' FizzBuzz. Macro calls can be parameters of other macro calls.
N 1 =
( 31 N. - ^
  P 0 =                                    ' P = 1 once something is printed
  #Z,#M,N.,3;; [ "Fizz" P 1 = ]
  #Z,#M,N.,5;; [ "Buzz" P 1 = ]
  1 P. - [ N. ! ]
  "!"
  N N. 1 + = )

$M %A %A %B / %B * - @                     ' M(a, b) = a mod b
$Z %A 1 + [ 1 %A - [ 1 @ ] ] 0 @           ' Z(a) = 1 if a = 0, otherwise 0
$$

name: lane-test
program:
' Tom Lane's test, from "Comment and Correction for Mouse", BYTE, June 1980.
' A sets its Q to 1, then runs its parameter, which calls B. B sets its own
' Q to 33. Each macro has its own variables, so A should print 1. The
' interpreter as published in 1979 prints 33.
#A,#B;;

$A Q 1 = %A Q. ! @
$B Q 33 = @
$$

name: grogono-hanoi
program:
' Listing 4 of Grogono's article: the Towers of Hanoi. The peg names are
' strings passed as parameters and handed on through the recursion.
"TOWERS OF HANOI!HOW MANY DISKS? " D ? = "!"
D. [ #H,D.,"LEFT","RIGHT","CENTER"; ]

$H %A [ #H,%A 1 -,%B,%D,%C;
        "MOVE " %B " TO " %C "!"
        #H,%A 1 -,%D,%C,%B; ] @
$$

name: grogono-bubble-sort
program:
' Listing 5 of Grogono's article: read an array, print it, bubble sort it
' and print it again. The main program uses no variables, so P can use
' all 26 of them as the array, reached through the address of A.
'   F is a FOR loop:  for %A := %B to %C do %D  (counting down if %B > %C)
'   E exchanges two variables given their addresses
"BUBBLE SORT!" #P,A;

$P "HOW MANY NUMBERS? " N ? = N. 26 - [ "TOO MANY!" @ ]
   "!ENTER " N. ! " NUMBERS!" N N. 1 - =
   #F,M,0,N., %A M. + ? =;
   "INPUT ARRAY!"  #F,M,0,N., %A M. + . ! " "; "!"
   #B,%A,0,N.;
   "SORTED ARRAY!" #F,M,0,N., %A M. + . ! " "; "!" @

$B #F,I,%B 1 +,%C,
     #F,J,%C,I.,
       %A J. 1 - + .  %A J. + .  -
         [ #E,%A J. +,%A J. 1 - +; ] ; ; @

$F %A %B = %C %A. - 1 +
   [ ( %C %A. - 1 + ^ %D %A %A. 1 + = ) @ ]
     ( %A. %C - 1 + ^ %D %A %A. 1 - = ) @

$E %A %B. %B %A. = = @
$$

name: ackermann
program:
' Ackermann's function. Parameters are re-evaluated on every use, so a
' recursive macro should copy them into local variables first.
M 0 =
( 3 M. - ^
  N 0 =
  ( 4 N. - ^
    "A(" M. ! "," N. ! ") = " #A,M.,N.; ! "!"
    N N. 1 + = )
  M M. 1 + = )

$A M %A = N %B =
   1 M. - [ N. 1 + @ ]                     ' m = 0: n + 1
   1 N. - [ #A,M. 1 -,1; @ ]               ' n = 0: A(m - 1, 1)
   #A,M. 1 -,#A,M.,N. 1 -;; @              ' A(m - 1, A(m, n - 1))
$$

name: array-reverse
program:
' Any letter can be used as an array: the address B + I is element I.
' Read numbers until a negative one, then print them backwards.
' This is Grogono's program, with the 25-element limit check.
"Enter numbers, ending with a negative one:!"
A 0 =
( B A. + ? =
  B A. + . 1 + ^                           ' stop on a negative number
  A A. 1 + =
  A. 25 - [ "ARRAY FULL!" 0 ^ ] )
( A. ^
  A A. 1 - =
  B A. + . ! " " )
"!"
$$

name: binary
program:
' Print numbers in binary with a recursive macro: the high bits first,
' then the last bit.
( "Number (0 to stop): " N ? = N. ^
  N. ! " = " #B,N.; " in binary!" )
"!"

$B %A [ #B,%A 2 /; %A %A 2 / 2 * - ! ] @
$$

name: call-by-name
program:
' An actual parameter is not evaluated when the macro is called. Its text
' is run every time the formal parameter appears, in the caller's context.
#T,"hello ";  "!"                          ' the string is printed three times
"Two numbers: " #S,?; ! "!"                ' ? is read twice
X 0 = #T,X X. 1 + =; "X = " X. ! "!"       ' the assignment happens three times

$T %A %A %A @
$S %A %A + @
$$

name: change
program:
' Make change with the fewest coins. A is passed by reference.
"Amount in pence: " A ? = "!"
#C,A,200; #C,A,100; #C,A,50; #C,A,20; #C,A,10; #C,A,5; #C,A,2; #C,A,1;

$C N %A. %B / =                            ' N := how many of this coin
   N. [ N. ! " x " %B ! "p!" ]
   %A %A. N. %B * - = @                    ' take them off the amount
$$

name: collatz
program:
' The Collatz sequence: halve even numbers, triple-and-add-one odd ones.
"Start: " N ? = "!"
S 0 =
( N. ! " "
  N. 1 - ^                                 ' stop when N reaches 1
  R N. N. 2 / 2 * - =                      ' R := N mod 2, before N changes
  R. [ N N. 3 * 1 + = ]
  1 R. - [ N N. 2 / = ]
  S S. 1 + = )
"!" S. ! " steps!"
$$

name: diamond
program:
' A diamond, using a macro that prints its second parameter %A times.
"Size: " N ? = "!"
I 1 =
( N. I. - 1 + ^
  #R,N. I. -," "; #R,2 I. * 1 -,"*"; "!"
  I I. 1 + = )
I N. 1 - =
( I. ^
  #R,N. I. -," "; #R,2 I. * 1 -,"*"; "!"
  I I. 1 - = )

$R K %A = ( K. ^ %B K K. 1 - = ) @
$$

name: digits
program:
' Take a number apart: digit sum, digit count and the digits reversed.
"Number: " N ? = "!"
S 0 = C 0 = R 0 =
( N. ^
  D N. N. 10 / 10 * - =                    ' D := last digit
  S S. D. + =
  C C. 1 + =
  R R. 10 * D. + =
  N N. 10 / = )
"digits:   " C. ! "!"
"sum:      " S. ! "!"
"reversed: " R. ! "!"
$$

name: even-odd
program:
' There is no remainder operator: N mod D is  N  N D / D *  -
( "Number (0 to stop): " N ? = N. ^
  R N. N. 2 / 2 * - =                      ' R := N mod 2
  N. !
  R. [ " is odd!" ]
  1 R. - [ " is even!" ] )
"!"
$$

name: for-loop
program:
' Grogono's FOR macro: #F,var,from,to,body; counts up or down.
' The body is an actual parameter, so it is run in the caller's context.
"Up:     " #F,I,1,10, I. ! " "; "!"
"Down:   " #F,I,10,1, I. ! " "; "!"
"Squares:" #F,I,1,8, " " I. I. * !; "!"
"Nested: " #F,I,1,3, #F,J,1,3, I. ! J. ! " ";; "!"

$F %A %B = %C %A. - 1 +
   [ ( %C %A. - 1 + ^ %D %A %A. 1 + = ) @ ]
     ( %A. %C - 1 + ^ %D %A %A. 1 - = ) @
$$

name: gcd
program:
' Greatest common divisor by Euclid's algorithm.
"First number: " A ? =
"Second number: " B ? = "!"
"gcd(" A. ! ", " B. ! ") = "
( B. ^
  T B. =
  B #M,A.,B.; =                            ' B := A mod B
  A T. = )
A. ! "!"

$M %A %A %B / %B * - @                     ' M(a, b) = a mod b
$$

name: grogono-factorial
program:
' From "Mouse: A Language for Microcomputers", Peter Grogono, BYTE July 1979.
' Asks for numbers and prints their factorials until given zero or less.
( "ENTER A NUMBER " M ? = M. ^
  N M. = 1 ( N. ^ N. * N N. 1 - = )
  "FACTORIAL (" M. ! ") = " ! "!" )
$$

name: grogono-green-bottles
program:
' Listing 3 of Grogono's article: a song, sung by a recursive macro.
' (A leading space has been added to W; the printed listing ran
' "BOTTLES" and "STANDING" together.)
( "HOW MANY VERSES? " S ? = S. ^
  "!" 10 S. - [ #V,S. 1 +; ] )

$V %A 1 - [ #N,%A; #B; #W; ",!"
            #N,%A; #B; ";!" #F; ",!"
            #N,%A 1 -; #B; #W; ".!!"
            #V,%A 1 -; ] @

$B " GREEN BOTTLES" @
$W " STANDING ON THE WALL" @
$F "IF ONE OF THOSE BOTTLES SHOULD HAPPEN TO FALL" @

$N %A 9 - [ "NINE"  @ ]
   %A 8 - [ "EIGHT" @ ]
   %A 7 - [ "SEVEN" @ ]
   %A 6 - [ "SIX"   @ ]
   %A 5 - [ "FIVE"  @ ]
   %A 4 - [ "FOUR"  @ ]
   %A 3 - [ "THREE" @ ]
   %A 2 - [ "TWO"   @ ]
   %A 1 - [ "ONE"   @ ]
   %A     [ "NO"    @ ] @
$$

name: grogono-parameters
program:
' From Grogono's article: missing parameters are empty, extra ones are
' ignored, and a call to an undefined macro (U) does nothing.
#T; #T,"A"; #T,"A","B"; #T,"A","B","C"; #U;

$T "<" %A %B ">!" @
$$

name: grogono-primes-endless
program:
' Listing 2 of Grogono's article, as printed: it prints prime numbers and
' never stops. Press Ctrl-C to end it. See primes.mouse for a version
' with a limit.
"PRIME NUMBERS!" N 1 = ( N N. 1 + = #P,N.; )

$P F 1 = N 1 =
   ( F F. 1 + = %A F. - ^ %A F. / F. * %A - 1 + [ N 0 = 0 ^ ] )
   N. [ %A ! "!" ] @
$$

name: grogono-squares-triangles
program:
' Listing 1 of Grogono's article: square and triangular numbers computed
' by two mutually recursive macros.
'   S(n) = T(n) + T(n-1),  T(n) = (S(n-1) + 3n - 1) / 2,  S(1) = T(1) = 1
"SQUARE AND TRIANGULAR NUMBERS!"
( "ENTER A NUMBER " N ? = N. ^
  "S(" N. ! ") = " #S,N.; !
  "   T(" N. ! ") = " #T,N.; ! "!" )

$S %A 1 - [ #T,%A; #T,%A 1 -; + @ ] 1 @
$T %A 1 - [ #S,%A 1 -; 3 %A * 1 - + 2 / @ ] 1 @
$$

name: leap-years
program:
' Leap years: divisible by 4, except centuries, except every fourth century.
( "Year (0 to stop): " Y ? = Y. ^
  L 0 =
  #Z,#M,Y.,4;;   [ L 1 = ]
  #Z,#M,Y.,100;; [ L 0 = ]
  #Z,#M,Y.,400;; [ L 1 = ]
  Y. !
  L. [ " is a leap year!" ]
  1 L. - [ " is not a leap year!" ] )
"!"

$M %A %A %B / %B * - @
$Z %A 1 + [ 1 %A - [ 1 @ ] ] 0 @
$$

name: locals
program:
' Every macro call has its own 26 variables. The main program's N is
' untouched by the N inside X. This is Grogono's example; it prints 3.
N 3 = #X; N. ! "!"

' Tom Lane's test from BYTE, June 1980: B is called while A's parameter is
' being evaluated and must not overwrite A's Q. The interpreter as first
' published printed 33; the corrected one prints 1.
#A,#B;; "!"

$X N 99 = @
$A Q 1 = %A Q. ! @
$B Q 33 = @
$$

name: max
program:
' A macro that leaves a value on the stack is a function.
"Three numbers: " A ? = B ? = C ? = "!"
"largest:  " #X,#X,A.,B.;,C.; ! "!"
"smallest: " #N,#N,A.,B.;,C.; ! "!"

$X %A %B - [ %A @ ] %B @                   ' X(a, b) = the larger
$N %B %A - [ %A @ ] %B @                   ' N(a, b) = the smaller
$$

name: multiplication-table
program:
' Nested loops. Numbers are printed with no padding, so pad by hand.
I 1 =
( 10 I. - ^
  J 1 =
  ( 10 J. - ^
    P I. J. * =
    10 P. - [ " " ]                        ' one more space if P < 10
    " " P. !
    J J. 1 + = )
  "!"
  I I. 1 + = )
$$

name: pascal-triangle
program:
' Pascal's triangle. Each entry comes from the one before it:
' C(n, k) = C(n, k - 1) * (n - k + 1) / k
N 0 =
( 9 N. - ^
  S 8 N. - = ( S. ^ " " S S. 1 - = )       ' indent
  C 1 = K 0 =
  ( N. K. - 1 + ^
    C. ! " "
    K K. 1 + =
    C C. N. K. - 1 + * K. / = )
  "!"
  N N. 1 + = )
$$

name: perfect-numbers
program:
' Perfect numbers: equal to the sum of their proper divisors.
N 2 =
( 500 N. - ^
  S 1 = D 2 =
  ( N. 2 / D. - 1 + ^                      ' for D := 2 to N / 2
    #Z,#M,N.,D.;; [ S S. D. + = ]
    D D. 1 + = )
  #Z,S. N. -; [ N. ! " is perfect!" ]
  N N. 1 + = )

$M %A %A %B / %B * - @
$Z %A 1 + [ 1 %A - [ 1 @ ] ] 0 @
$$

name: power
program:
' Fast exponentiation by squaring. T is local to each call of P.
"Base: " B ? = "Exponent: " E ? = "!"
B. ! "^" E. ! " = " #P,B.,E.; ! "!"

$P %B [ T #P,%A,%B 2 /; =                  ' T := base ^ (exp / 2)
        %B %B 2 / 2 * - [ T. T. * %A * @ ] ' odd exponent
        T. T. * @ ]
   1 @                                     ' anything ^ 0 = 1
$$

name: primes
program:
' Primes up to a limit, by trial division. Based on Grogono's listing 2.
"Primes up to: " L ? = "!"
N 2 =
( L. N. - 1 + ^
  #P,N.;
  N N. 1 + = )
"!"

$P F 1 = N 1 =                             ' N = 1 while %A still looks prime
   ( F F. 1 + =
     %A F. F. * - 1 + ^                    ' stop once F * F > %A
     %A F. / F. * %A - 1 + [ N 0 = 0 ^ ] ) ' F divides %A: not prime
   N. [ %A ! " " ] @
$$

name: roman-numerals
program:
' Roman numerals. The first parameter is passed by reference (N, not N.)
' so the macro can change the caller's variable.
( "Number (0 to stop): " N ? = N. ^
  N. ! " = "
  #R,N,1000,"M"; #R,N,900,"CM"; #R,N,500,"D"; #R,N,400,"CD";
  #R,N,100,"C";  #R,N,90,"XC";  #R,N,50,"L";  #R,N,40,"XL";
  #R,N,10,"X";   #R,N,9,"IX";   #R,N,5,"V";   #R,N,4,"IV";
  #R,N,1,"I";
  "!" )
"!"

$R ( %A. %B - 1 + ^                        ' while value >= %B
     %C                                    ' print the numeral
     %A %A. %B - = ) @                     ' and subtract it
$$

name: square-root
program:
' Integer square root by Newton's method.
( "Number (0 to stop): " N ? = N. ^
  X N. =
  ( Y X. N. X. / + 2 / =                   ' Y := (X + N / X) / 2
    X. Y. - ^                              ' stop when it no longer shrinks
    X Y. = )
  "isqrt(" N. ! ") = " X. ! "!" )
"!"
$$

name: statistics
program:
' Count, total, largest, smallest and mean of a list ending with 0.
"Enter positive numbers, ending with 0:!"
C 0 = S 0 = H 0 = L 0 =
( N ? = N. ^
  C C. 1 + =
  S S. N. + =
  N. H. - [ H N. = ]                       ' new largest
  1 C. - 1 + [ L N. = ]                    ' first number is the smallest so far
  L. N. - [ L N. = ] )                     ' new smallest
C. [ "count:    " C. ! "!"
     "total:    " S. ! "!"
     "largest:  " H. ! "!"
     "smallest: " L. ! "!"
     "mean:     " S. C. / ! "!" ]
$$

name: swap
program:
' Grogono's trick: exchange two variables using the stack, no temporary.
X 1 = Y 2 =
"Before: X = " X. ! ", Y = " Y. ! "!"
X Y. Y X. = =
"After:  X = " X. ! ", Y = " Y. ! "!"
$$

name: temperature
program:
' Fahrenheit to Celsius, in whole degrees.
"  F    C!"
F 0 =
( 221 F. - ^
  C F. 32 - 5 * 9 / =
  100 F. - [ " " ] 10 F. - [ " " ]         ' right-align F in three columns
  F. ! "   " C. ! "!"
  F F. 20 + = )
$$

name: triangle
program:
' A triangle of stars.
"Height: " H ? = "!"
R 1 =
( H. R. - 1 + ^
  C R. =
  ( C. ^ "*" C C. 1 - = )
  "!"
  R R. 1 + = )
$$
